prompt:
A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Berkelium (버클륨) itself — the sovereign of the Berkelium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: about twenty — a youthful face; no facial lines.
Face — her own: a sharp, striking, intense look; fair skin; oval face; eyes on the larger side of natural — peach-blossom eyes with a soft, curved lower lid, level outer eye corners; gracefully arched brows; petite straight nose; lips with a defined cupid's bow, of natural size; steel-blue eyes; a small beauty mark under one eye.
Body and hair: willowy and long-limbed with soft curves — a full bust, rounded hips and a slender waist build; three high ponytails fanning out with wispy see-through bangs; deep scholar's navy hair threaded with fine bright gold strands like a graduation tassel.
Hair: her hair is worn exactly as described above — loose, long or cut as named; do not pin it up into a bun or tuck it under goggles or a hat unless the hair above is an updo.
Expression: a composed, self-assured look.
Her element, carried in her design: berkelium: a soft silvery synthetic metal first made in late 1949 by striking americium with alpha particles, and named for the university town where she was born, just as terbium above her was named for a small village; the town itself was named for a philosopher who taught that to exist is to be perceived, and at first she existed only as the decay of a few atoms, until more than a decade later a speck large enough to see was gathered; in water she turns yellow and pale green, and in 2009 a few precious milligrams of her, gathered over months in a reactor, were flown across an ocean to another laboratory to become the target that made element 117.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — STEAMPUNK
Costume: late-Victorian industrial dress — a high-necked blouse with a waistcoat or a tailored tail coat, leather gloves, a work apron or utility belt with brass fittings, goggles hung at the neck or a small instrument as ornament; below, a short bustle skirt and laced boots; the traits above as colour accents. No crown unless the opening line says she wears one; steam, pipes and gauges in the scene.
Silhouette: a fitted bodice and a long bustled ball gown sweeping out behind her, long gloves — an elegant, wide-trailing shape. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Colours: scholar's deep navy, tassel gold, berkelium-salt pale yellow-green, chalk-white stone.
Exposure (bold): her outfit opens to show skin — the neckline opened down to the sternum with natural cleavage, bare forearms, and bare legs above the boots or through a high slit where the silhouette allows; pieces stay symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: around 1914, a college town on a hillside above a wide bay: the commencement ball in a great domed hall on the day the new white bell tower is first lit, electric chandeliers over a polished floor, groves of tall eucalyptus outside, and a golden strait glowing at sunset beyond the bay.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: bright warm sunlight with soft sky light bounced from white clouds.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Bk) and atomic number (97) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish, armor plates, cape, modern plastic, sci-fi.
